rules.title: Boston fair housing ban on discrimination in renting, including against rental assistance recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on protected characteristics, including rental assistance (e.g., Section 8 vouchers), family status, and military status. Refusing to accept rental assistance is an example of prohibited discrimination.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any housing rented, bought, sold, or financed in the City of Boston. Protected classes listed: race, color, religion, disability, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, marital status, rental assistance, family status, military status.
rules.citation: City of Boston fair housing law, enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission (specific code section not stated in source)
rules.quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.
rules.conflict_note: Summary page does not give an ordinance citation, effective date, or any exemptions; it also states the commission enforces state and federal fair housing laws, so the specific source of each protection is not identified.
